Personally, I think there should be some serious reconsiderations about the current curriculum to improve the current situation. First of all, the aim of this course should be determined. If the purpose of this course is to give some sense of "linear algebra and differential equations" to students in an introductory manner, then the way of teaching should be changed. For the linear algebra part, even though the name includes "algebra", I think what is going on in this lecture is pure geometry and there is lack of emphasis about this fact. Rather than thinking about the matrices and those methods, I think the focus should be on what those matrices and linear systems actually tell. Once we get the idea behind those systems by considering them as an information about vectors, all of those elimination methods etc. becomes something we can imagine and make sense of it. Textbook includes proofs for those methods in a rigorous mathematical way for sure, yet, it lacks to convey information about what is going on in the background, so everything becomes an algorithm that we must apply without grasping anything. This is neither what mathematics is nor the purpose of this course. If we are expected to understand and apply rigorous proofs properly then 8 weeks is simply not enough for a topic like linear algebra. But if the purpose is to give some sense, then I think the geometric interpretation of all of those linear combinations etc. carry a lot importance to visualize what is going on. For the differential equations part, I don't have much right to talk about because I haven't attended to the lectures but I think it's tough to "teach" differential equations only within 6 weeks for any instructor. Also, this time constraint turns the lecture into an exam oriented one rather than teaching something. If this happens in a math lecture, my personal opinion is that it's quite expected to see average GPA of 1.10's because one can't solve anything without grasping the idea.
